newsitem.title: POLAND: Deutsche Bank Polska sees break-even in '97.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank Polska sees break-even in '97.

text.p: Deutsche Bank Polska SA, the year-old Polish subsidiary of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, will reach break-even next year and aims to open branches outside Warsaw, its chairman Georg Krupp said on Tuesday.
"In the second year of our activity in Poland, in 1997, we will reach break-even," Krupp told a news conference.
He said the bank would consider opening branches in Poznan, Gdansk, Szczecin, Katowice and Wroclaw.
Although Deutsche Bank Polska (DBP) had a sophisticated electronic banking system working in Poland, it wanted direct contact with clients beyond its Warsaw base, he said.

"We see big possibilities in leasing and in operations on the capital market in Poland," he said. "In a further perspective, we also aim to offer savings systems for financing construction and insurance systems on this market," he added.

He said that for the home and insurance businesses, the bank would use Deutsche Bank AG's German subsidiaries. However for leasing, the bank would set up a leasing company in Poland, in cooperation with Deutsche Bank group's trade credit firm GEFA.
"Leasing in Poland is comparatively weakly developed and we anticipate that it will soon grow dynamically," he said.
The bank also was issuing Eurocard Gold and Eurocard Business credit cards, he added.

Officials said the bank had tripled its own capital to 135 million zlotys from 45 million and was one of the few banks in Poland to have access to long-term funds from the Luxembourg-based European Investment Bank.
